page: Amazon Web Services i2.4xlarge is a storage-optimized second-generation instance utilizing the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor with an x86_64 architecture, featuring 8 physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs via hyperthreading. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz and includes 25 MB of L3 cache. The hardware configuration includes 122.0 GB of system memory, yielding 7.62 GB per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 3200 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance across several core compute and memory metrics. The instance achieves average ratings in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, alongside average PassMark CPU and memory scores. Read-only memory bandwidth is average, reaching 588.91 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 41.79 GB/sec for large blocks. However, write bandwidth for large blocks is weak at 18.74 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression are weak, while single-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the poor category. Geekbench testing shows poor single-core and weak multi-core performance, though specific tasks like software compilation and ray tracing maintain average marks. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 6.04 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput averages 14.27 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the i2.4xlarge is its reliance on older Intel Xeon architecture, which limits its single-core processing efficiency and instruction set capabilities, lacking newer AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Qualitatively, the instance offers high local storage density and memory capacity relative to its compute power, making it cost-efficient for storage-intensive workloads that do not require modern CPU instruction sets. It is suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis, static web serving, and legacy storage-heavy applications.
description: Amazon Web Services i2.4xlarge is a storage-optimized instance featuring 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It includes 122.0 GB of system memory and 3200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, operating on the Xen hypervisor with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data shows average performance in multi-core CPU tests, PassMark database operations, and Redis SET operations, though single-core execution and large-block memory write speeds are weak. Lacking modern AVX-512 extensions, the instance presents a tradeoff between raw processing power and high local storage capacity. It is best suited for database hosting, caching layers, and storage-heavy workloads that benefit from dense local NVMe storage.
